title: WHOSE OPINIONS MATTER? PERSPECTIVE-AWARE MODELS TO IDENTIFY OPINIONS OF HATE SPEECH VICTIMS IN ABUSIVE LANGUAGE DETECTION
measurement_description: The paper measured the presence of hate speech, aggressiveness, offensiveness, and stereotypes against religious groups, with a specific focus on Islamophobia (abusive language targeting Muslims). It evaluated how different annotator groups (victims vs. non-victims) perceive such content.
findings: The paper found that opinions on abusive language related to Islam are highly polarized. The 'Target' group, which included first- or second-generation immigrants of Muslim background, consistently identified more content as hateful and aggressive compared to the 'Control' group of researchers. The most polarizing tweets frequently contained keywords related to 'Muslim invasion', 'radical Islam', 'terrorism', and 'rapists'. The proposed perspective-aware models, trained on data partitioned by annotator group, were better able to capture these different viewpoints and improved classification performance over a baseline model trained on aggregated data.
references: M. Duggan. Online harassment 2017. Technical report, Pew Research Center., 2017.
